newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise, tracking U.S. market.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise, tracking U.S. market.

text.p: Argentine bonds were slightly higher late Thursday after having followed U.S. Treasuries first lower and then higher.
The market remained thin amid caution ahead of the policy-making Federal Open Market Committee meeting March 25.
"Volume remains thin because of the caution" on U.S. rates, said one trader.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 1/8 to 89-3/4, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.15 to 126.40.
"Many portfolios have already been reduced as a defensive measure against a possible change in U.S. rates," said another trader.
Market players said the balance for a rate hike rose this session after statements by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, who said the economy retains a "great deal of vigor."
Traders said the market was set to take its direction from U.S. markets again on Friday.
In the money markets, call money rates were flat at 5.93 percent.
